name: ASCII1D
description: ASCII.SANS.1D module list (coach M1): moving 1D SAS data in four directions — file to table, table to file, file to file, table to table — with the module's options on the way; synthetic input files written by the setup.
instruction: Use exactly the object names given. End the item by printing exactly ONE line: the result label the item gives, then only the values asked for, in the order asked, separated by spaces.
setup: import os, shutil base = os.path.expanduser("~/benchdata") shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True) for sub in ("in", "multi", "out", "converted"): os.makedirs(os.path.join(base, sub)) def write(path, lines): with open(os.path.join(base, path), "w") as f: f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n") # plain: 20 points, Q = 0.01 k, I = 2 k, dI = 0.1, sigma = 0.001 write("in/plain.dat", ["%.4f %.4f 0.1 0.001" % (0.01 * k, 2.0 * k) for k in range(1, 21)]) # opt: the same data, for the items with options (their tables do not replace item 1's) write("in/opt.dat", ["%.4f %.4f 0.1 0.001" % (0.01 * k, 2.0 * k) for k in range(1, 21)]) # header: 5 text lines, then 10 points Q = 0.02 k, I = 10 + k, dI = 0.5 write("in/header.dat", ["# sample: header test", "# instrument: synthetic", "# date: 2026-10-19", "# columns: Q I dI", "# end of header"] + ["%.4f %.4f 0.5" % (0.02 * k, 10.0 + k) for k in range(1, 11)]) # GRASP-like: a header with numeric lines, data after "***** Data *****": 15 points Q = 0.005 k, I = 50 - k write("in/grasp.dat", ["GRASP_Variant V.10.24c Instrument: SYNTHETIC", "", "Beam Centre1 : Cx = 64.4493 Cy = 64.1428", "Transmissions: Ts = 0.94823 +/- 0.0015088", "Sample-Det1 Dist (m): 1.1115", "Wavelength: 4.5, Delta Wav: 0.1", "", "***** Data *****", "Mod_Q\tI\tErr_I\tSigma_Q", ""] + ["%.5f\t%.4f\t0.2\t0.0008" % (0.005 * k, 50.0 - k) for k in range(1, 16)]) # canSAS 1D XML: 8 points Q = 0.01 k, I = 5 k, Idev = 0.5, Qdev = 0.001 points = "".join('%.3f%.1f0.5' '0.001\n' % (0.01 * k, 5.0 * k) for k in range(1, 9)) write("in/cansas.xml", ['', '', "synthetic", points + ""]) # a folder of three runs: 10 points each, Q = 0.01 k, I = run * k for run in (101, 102, 103): write("multi/run_%d.dat" % run, ["%.4f %.4f 0.1" % (0.01 * k, run * k) for k in range(1, 11)]) # two tables for table -> table: QI-alpha (I = k), QI-beta (I = 3 k), 10 rows, Q = 0.01 k for name, f in (("QI-alpha", 1.0), ("QI-beta", 3.0)): t = newTable(name, 10, 3) t.setColData(1, [0.01 * k for k in range(1, 11)]) t.setColData(2, [f * k for k in range(1, 11)]) t.setColData(3, [0.1] * 10)

items.text: Import the SANS curve plain.dat from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory into the project. Print the name of the table made, its number of rows, the first Q and the sum of I.
items.hint: the default table name comes from the module's name structure (reference script decides)
items.verify:
made = [table(n) for n in tableNames() if "plain" in n]
check(any(t.numRows() == 20 and abs(sum(t.colData(2)) - 420) < 1e-9 for t in made))

items.text: Import the ascii file header.dat from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory as the table "HeaderData"; it starts with a 5-line text header. Print the number of rows and the first Q of "HeaderData".

Import the radially averaged dataset grasp.dat from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory, a GRASP output whose data start after the line "***** Data *****". Print the number of rows and the first and last Q.
items.hint: a header line with two numbers (Cx/Cy, Wavelength) read as a data point
items.verify:
t = table([n for n in tableNames() if "grasp" in n][0])
check(t.numRows(), t.cell(1, 1), t.cell(1, t.numRows()))

items.text: Import the SAS data file cansas.xml (canSAS 1D XML) from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory. Print the number of rows, the sum of I and the dI of the first point.
items.hint: the XML read as plain ASCII
items.verify:
t = table([n for n in tableNames() if "cansas" in n][0])
check(t.numRows(), sum(t.colData(2)))

items.text: Import all 1D SANS files (.dat) of the folder benchdata/multi in the home directory, one table each. Print how many tables were made and the sum of I of the one made from run_102.dat.
items.hint: only one file imported, or the files merged
items.verify: check(len([n for n in tableNames() if "run" in n and "101" in n or "run" in n and "102" in n or "run" in n and "103" in n]) >= 3)

items.text: Export the SANS table made from plain.dat in item 1 as an ascii file to the folder benchdata/out in the home directory, with the file extension RAD. Print the name of the file written (without its folder) and its number of data lines.
items.hint: the file name printed with its folder, or a header line written

items.text: Export the SAS dataset QI-alpha to the folder benchdata/out in the home directory as the file alpha3.dat, with 3 columns only (Q, I, dI — no sigma). Print the number of numbers on its first data line.
items.verify:
import os
f = os.path.expanduser("~/benchdata/out/alpha3.dat")
line = [l for l in open(f) if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")][0]
check(len(line.split()))

items.text: Import opt.dat from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory as a new table, this time removing the first 2 and the last 5 points. Print the number of rows and the first and last Q of the new table.
items.hint: points removed after the import instead of by the module, or the wrong ends cut

items.text: Import opt.dat from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory and convert it to the Kratky presentation (I·Q² vs Q) with the module's automatic name prefix. Print the name of the Kratky table and its value at the third point.
items.hint: Guinier or Porod chosen instead of Kratky
items.verify:
ks = [n for n in tableNames() if n.startswith("Kratky")]
check(len(ks) > 0, round(table(ks[0]).cell(2, 3), 6))

Print sigma at the first point with 6 significant digits.

items.text: Import opt.dat from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory with I multiplied by 2 and then a background of 0.01 subtracted. Print the sum of the new I with 2 decimals.
Import opt.dat from the folder benchdata/in in the home directory with linear binning of every 3 points. Print the number of rows and the first Q and first I of the binned table.
